feature.title: Notes
feature.problem: A reader who finds something useful in the library has nowhere to put it. They screenshot the screen and lose it in the camera roll, so the app is where things are found and somewhere else is where they are kept.
nonGoals: Sharing a note with another account — a note is private until there is a reason for it not to be.
Rich text. A note that needs formatting is a document, and this is not a document editor.

surfaces.name: Notes
surfaces.purpose: everything the reader kept, newest first

moments.peak: The list is already there — the note they came back for is the top row, not something they have to search for.
moments.end: A pull refreshes and the list settles without moving what they were reading.

states.loading: Six skeleton rows, the same height as a real one.
states.empty: Nothing kept yet. Save something from the library.
states.success: The list renders and a pull refreshes it.

panels.title: Note
rows: extendBody runs the content under the
bar, which is what gives the glass

moments.peak: The note reads like a page, not a record: the text is the widest thing on the screen.
moments.end: The bar is still under their thumb when they reach the bottom, so editing is one tap away.

states.loading: The title renders from the row that opened it; the body is bones.
states.empty: An empty note reads Nothing written yet.
states.error: This note could not be opened.
states.success: The note renders and the pinned bar stays put while it scrolls.

moments.peak: The cursor is already in the body — they type the first word without aiming at anything.
moments.end: Save returns to the note with their words on it, so the edit is visibly kept.

states.loading: The fields render disabled until the note arrives.
states.empty: A new note opens with the title focused.
states.error: This note could not be saved. Nothing was lost.
states.success: Save returns to the note with the new text on it.

overlays.title: Delete this note?
overlays.body: Deleting removes it from every device signed in to this account.

overlays.title: Sort notes
overlays.body: Newest first, oldest first, or by title.

components.why: Archive is the common action, and a swipe is the gesture a reader already has for it.
components.rejected: a trailing icon button on every row

components.why: The swipe's tappable twin. Without it the action is invisible to VoiceOver.
Edit must not scroll away on a long note.
components.rejected: a FAB, which covers the last line of the body

components.why: It owns the label-above/helper-below contract, so validation does not move the layout.
